US/MA/south-coast.name: South Coast
US/MA/south-coast.notes: The Fall River, New Bedford and Dartmouth area of south-eastern Massachusetts. An informal region with no government. Only the member places present in the registry are listed under covers.

adjacent_unmapped.name: Dartmouth, Massachusetts
adjacent_unmapped.note: To the east. Usually counted as part of the Farm Coast.

US/RI/bristol.name: Bristol
US/RI/bristol.notes: County seat of Bristol County, on a peninsula between Narragansett Bay and Mount Hope Bay. Joined to Portsmouth by the Mount Hope Bridge; the Prudence Island ferry leaves from here. Shares a school district and a water authority with Warren.

US/RI/middletown.name: Middletown
US/RI/middletown.notes: On Aquidneck Island between Portsmouth to the north and Newport to the south. Shares a school-regionalization discussion with Newport.

US/RI/newport-county.name: Newport County
US/RI/newport-county.notes: Rhode Island counties have no government of their own; the county is a geographic and statistical area. Regional sources are filed here.

US/RI/portsmouth.name: Portsmouth
US/RI/portsmouth.notes: On Aquidneck Island, joined to Tiverton by the Sakonnet River Bridge. Includes Prudence, Patience, Hope and Hog islands.

adjacent_unmapped.name: Fall River, Massachusetts
adjacent_unmapped.note: To the north, across the state line.

US/RI/warren.name: Warren

adjacent_unmapped.name: Swansea, Massachusetts
adjacent_unmapped.note: To the east, across the state line.

US/RI/warren.notes: Between Bristol and Barrington on the east side of Narragansett Bay. Shares a school district (filed under Bristol) and a water authority (filed under Bristol County) with Bristol.

US/farm-coast.name: Farm Coast
US/farm-coast.notes: A name used locally for the coastal farming towns on both sides of the Rhode Island and Massachusetts line. It crosses a state border, which is why it is filed directly under the country. Dartmouth, MA is usually included and is not yet in the registry.
